youtube.title: All the water in one ball | Possibility Lab Season 2 · Episode 5
youtube.caption:
How big is Earth's water? Gather every drop into one ball, and measure it.

All of Earth's water, liquid, ice and vapor together, is about 1.386 billion cubic kilometers. Squeezed into one ball, it is about 1,400 km wide: 40% of the Moon's width and 11% of the Earth's. Only the fresh water makes a ball about 400 km wide. Its share of the Earth's volume is only about an eighth of one percent.

Series: Season 2, episode 5 of 6.

Sources
1. The USGS total counts all of Earth's water: oceans, ice caps and glaciers, groundwater, lakes, soil moisture, atmosphere, rivers and living things. — usgs.gov: https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school/science/how-much-water-there-earth
2. Total water on Earth is about 1,386,000,000 km3 (332.5 million cubic miles), from Gleick (1996) as shown by USGS. — usgs.gov: https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school/science/how-much-water-there-earth
3. Sphere diameter d = (6 V / pi)^(1/3) = 1,383 km for V = 1.386e9 km3. — Derivation (no outside page; arithmetic shown in the film)
4. 1,383 km / 3,480 km (Moon diameter) = 40%. — NASA: https://science.nasa.gov/moon/facts/
5. 1,383 km / 12,756 km = 0.108: a 24 cm basketball next to a 2.6 cm ball (a large marble). — Derivation (no outside page; arithmetic shown in the film)
6. About 2.5% of Earth's water is fresh; 1.386e9 x 0.025 = 3.5e7 km3 gives a ball 404 km wide. — usgs.gov: https://www.usgs.gov/special-topics/water-science-school/science/how-much-water-there-earth
7. 1.386e9 km3 / 1.087e12 km3 (Earth's volume) = 0.13%, about one-eighth of one percent. — Derivation (no outside page; arithmetic shown in the film)
8. Spread evenly over the whole Earth the water would be about 2.7 km deep (1.386e9 km3 / 5.1e8 km2 of surface); the film in the picture is 1.2% of the radius, 76 km: about 28 times thicker. — Derivation (no outside page; arithmetic shown in the film)
9. The Earth's equatorial diameter is 12,756 km. — NASA: https://science.nasa.gov/earth/facts/

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Animation: code-rendered, no stock footage. Every number is checked against the sources.

Possibility Lab: Impossible questions, honest assumptions, real calculations.
